sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area (Pacific Linguistics D-90). Index entry 'Senggi (S of Jayapura)'.
sources.note: Index: 'Senggi (S of Jayapura) Barrs 1978, Galis 1956, Laycock 1973, SH, Voorhoeve 1975, W&H 1981' - all surveys/wordlists; Galis 1956 = Ethnografische notities over het Senggi-gebied, Hollandia: Kantoor Bevolkingszaken, 32 pp. No phonological work listed.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. TransNewGuinea.org: language page 'Viid' (127 lexical items from Voorhoeve 1971/1975).
sources.note: Wordlist forms only (e.g. aŋgla 'arm', tokos 'ashes'), no stress marks, no prosodic note.
Cites Voorhoeve 1971: 60-68, Loving & Bass 1964: 4, Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). No grammar, sketch or phonology reference exists for the language.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: Senggi (Northwest New Guinea > Tami River-Bewani Range).
Hammarström, Harald & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2012. The languages of Melanesia: quantifying the level of coverage. LD&C Special Publication 5, online appendix, entry 'Senggi [snu] < Border, Warisic'.
sources.note: Lists every known source: Galis 1955 [overview, wordlist]; Galis 1956b 'Etnographische notities over het Senggi-gebied' [ethnographic, wordlist]; Laycock 1973 [overview]; Menanti 2005 'Laporan Sosiolinguistik Bahasa Viid di Kampung Senggi' to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports [overview, wordlist, socling]; Voorhoeve 1971. Nothing above wordlist level; no phonology.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-224 [snu]: add name Viid (submitted by Randy Lebold, SIL, 2007-08-29).
sources.note: Only reports that the autonym is Viid, from an SIL rapid appraisal survey of March 2005. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry no. 105 SENGGI (pp. 43-44): ±120 speakers, villages Senggi, Tomfor, Umbekwai; sources Galis 1956a (wordlist), Voorhoeve 1971, Laycock 1973. Wordlist conventions p. 91: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.' Senggi comparative wordlist (from Galis) carries no stress marks. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'The Tami stock' pp. 60-68 (the pages Glottolog cites for Senggi). p. 61: 'SENGGI was, in 1956, spoken in three villages... The only data on hand is the wordlist collected by Galis (1956a).' Sec. 2.3.3 Phonology (pp. 62-64) analyses Awji, Taikat, Manem and Waris only and never mentions stress or accent; Senggi appears once (p. 64: final consonant clusters 'also found in the other members of the Waris family, Senggi and Waina'). Silent on stress for every language, and no Senggi phonology at all.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). Peta Bahasa: Bahasa Senggi (Find), Provinsi Papua.
sources.note: Location and dialectometry only (97.75-99.75% difference from Jorop and Yabanda). No phonology, no stress.
Stub and classification pages; no phonology. Border family described only as lacking gender/number.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Menanti, Jackie. 2005. Laporan Sosiolinguistik Bahasa Viid di Kampung Senggi, Kabupaten Keerom, Papua - Indonesia. SIL Indonesia rapid-appraisal survey report (listed as 'to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports').

sources.note: The only post-1960 primary fieldwork on the language (SIL survey, March 2005, source of the autonym Viid); SIL survey reports carry a wordlist and sometimes phonetic transcription notes that could mark stress. Not found in the SIL archive or Google Books; may be unpublished.
